clinician.trajectory_summary: A 7-year-old girl presented with painless bilateral mydriasis and absent light reflexes for 7 days, following a mild upper respiratory infection. Initial neurological examination, head CT, CSF analysis, and nerve conduction studies were unremarkable. However, serum anti-GQ1b and anti-GT1a antibodies were positive. She was treated with IVIG, leading to normalization of pupil diameter and restored light reflexes within 5 days, with sustained resolution at 6-month follow-up without developing classic MFS features.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with painless bilateral mydriasis and absent light reflexes for 7 days, following a mild upper respiratory infection.
Initial neurological exam showed intact cranial nerves, normal muscle tone/strength, gait, coordination, and normoactive deep tendon reflexes.
Serum anti-GQ1b (IgM/IgG) and anti-GT1a (IgG) antibodies were positive.
Patient received IVIG 400 mg/kg/day for 5 days.
Post-treatment, pupil diameter normalized with restored light reflexes within 5 days, and resolution was sustained at 6-month follow-up without recurrence or development of classic MFS features.
